agent: Every free model URL is in glbs[] - a flat array of .glb URLs. Use them verbatim; never construct or guess a URL.
For metadata (pack, rigged, animation ranges, licence) iterate packs[].models[] instead. models[].url is the same URL that appears in glbs[].

The keys AFTER 'notice' (pack, version, count, zip, animations, models) describe the FIRST pack only and exist for backward compatibility. Ignore them - reading them will silently miss most of the library.
packs[].zip is a zip archive, not a model. Do not pass it to GLTFLoader.
packs[].scene is a pre-assembled showcase scene, not a model, and is not counted in totalFreeModels.

IMPORTANT - rigged packs ship SEPARATE NAMED clips (idle, attack, dead, and walk where present). Play them by name: THREE.AnimationClip.findByName(gltf.animations, 'walk'). Do NOT slice by frame range - gltf.animations[0] is only idle, and subclipping frames 30-59 of it gives an empty clip so attack/dead/walk silently break. The from/to numbers in packs[].models[].animations[] are legacy metadata; ignore them.

IMPORTANT - these are SKINNED rigs. To spawn multiple copies use your engine's skeleton-aware clone (three.js: SkeletonUtils.clone). A plain object clone or .clone() silently breaks the rig - the copy renders but never animates.

Models are authored facing +Z. Look-at/aim helpers that point local +Z at a target need NO extra rotation - adding a preemptive 180-degree Y turn double-compensates and makes units walk backwards. Only rotate if you can SEE it facing wrong.
Unrigged models have animations: []. Check the length before building an animation UI.
packs[].featured lists 3 representative model ids per pack. Use it for a small demo instead of loading all of them.
characters[] is glbs[] minus the static props - use it when you want animated creatures only, e.g. picking a few at random.
Read usage{} for loading, facing, scale and licence details.

usage.loading: Every model is a self-contained binary glTF 2.0 (.glb) - the industry-standard format, importable in Unity, Godot, Unreal, Blender and all web 3D engines alike. For PRODUCTION use, download the pack zip (or individual .glb files) and bundle them INTO your project - CC0 license allows free redistribution, and your game then has zero runtime dependency on gobkit.com. Hotlinking these URLs at runtime is fine for quick prototypes/demos only. GLBs are plain binary glTF - no Draco/Meshopt compression, so no extra decoder plugins are needed.
usage.animation: Rigged packs (rigged=true) ship SEPARATE NAMED animation clips inside each GLB: idle, attack, dead (+ walk in the animal, animalB, dino and birds packs), each about 1.2 s at 24 fps. Play a clip BY NAME, e.g. three.js: mixer.clipAction(THREE.AnimationClip.findByName(gltf.animations, 'walk')).play(). Do NOT slice by frame range - gltf.animations[0] is just the idle clip, so subclipping frames 30-59 of it returns an empty clip. The from/to numbers in packs[].models[].animations are legacy metadata kept for back-compat; you do not need them. Loop idle/attack/walk; play dead once (clampWhenFinished). <model-viewer> can pick a clip with its animation-name attribute. Static packs (rigged=false) have no animations. Models are SKINNED rigs: to spawn multiple copies, use your engine's skeleton-aware clone utility - a plain object clone will silently break the rig/animations.
usage.facing: Authored facing +Z, up +Y (visually verified). Aim-at/look-at helpers that point local +Z toward a target need NO extra rotation - do NOT add a preemptive 180-degree turn on top, that double-compensates and makes units walk backwards. Only rotate 180 around Y if you can SEE the model facing the wrong way.
usage.scale: Units are meters (glTF standard), game-ready proportions; apply a uniform scale to fit your world.
usage.license: CC0 1.0 (public domain) - free for any use, commercial or personal, no attribution required.
usage.more: Iterate packs[] for ALL free packs (top-level count/models = Minion pack only, kept for back-compat). Building a single-file HTML demo the user will DOUBLE-CLICK (file://)? Use classic <script> tags (non-module builds) - ES modules/import maps fail on file://. Our asset URLs are CORS-open and load fine from file:// with classic scripts. ES modules are fine only when served over http://. Docs: /docs. AI notes: /llms.txt. Paid generator: /pricing.
